Adopting AI with Red Hat Services Example use cases Next steps </a:ln></p:spPr></p:cxnSp><p:sp><p:nvSpPr><p:cNvPr id="7802" name="Google Shape;7802;p575"/><p:cNvSpPr txBox="1"/><p:nvPr/></p:nvSpPr><p:spPr><a:xfrm><a:off x="6037367" y="926167"/><a:ext cx="6392400" cy="737700"/></a:xfrm><a:prstGeom prst="rect"><a:avLst/></a:prstGeom><a:noFill/><a:ln><a:noFill/></a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="t" bIns="0" lIns="0" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="0" wrap="square" tIns="0"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:lnSpc><a:spcPct val="130000"/></a:lnSpc><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:rPr lang="en" sz="3700"><a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="000000"/></a:solidFill><a:latin typeface="Red Hat Display"/><a:ea typeface="Red Hat Display"/><a:cs typeface="Red Hat Display"/><a:sym typeface="Red Hat Display"/></a:rPr><a:t>What we’ll discuss today [Insert name of prospect company here] Our Red Hat experts bring proven blueprints to help you build new skills, high performing teams to develop innovative solutions to achieve your AI goals.

‹#› The Gen AI paradox: widespread adoption, untapped potential The rush to deploy GenAI is outpacing organizations’ readiness to operationalize it </a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="85975" lIns="85975" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="85975" wrap="square" tIns="85975"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> </a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="85975" lIns="85975" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="85975" wrap="square" tIns="85975"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> </a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="85975" lIns="85975" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="85975" wrap="square" tIns="85975"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> Data quality and preparation GenAI models require clean, well-structured, and reliable data to perform effectively. Perceived effort required to prepare internal data for these models is often underestimated. Technology and integration hurdles Organizations face challenges with integrating into ecosystems, scalability, security, and governance. The initial pilot often fails to address the robust requirements for a full-scale deployment. Lack of clear business use case Projects often lack a tangible return on investment (ROI) or clear path to value creation. Many pilots are launched out of enthusiasm without solving a specific, quantifiable business need. Despite being the most deployed AI solution within customer organizations, the vast majority of pilots are failing to reach full-scale production due to several key root causes 95% Highlighting a major gap between initial experimentation and successful production Source: MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing of Generative AI pilots fail*

</a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="91425" lIns="91425" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="91425" wrap="square" tIns="91425"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> </a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="91425" lIns="91425" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="91425" wrap="square" tIns="91425"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> </a:ln></p:spPr><p:txBody><a:bodyPr anchorCtr="0" anchor="ctr" bIns="91425" lIns="91425" spcFirstLastPara="1" rIns="91425" wrap="square" tIns="91425"><a:noAutofit/></a:bodyPr><a:lstStyle/><a:p><a:pPr indent="0" lvl="0" marL="0" rtl="0" algn="l"><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcBef><a:spcAft><a:spcPts val="0"/></a:spcAft><a:buNone/></a:pPr><a:r><a:t> ‹#› The future of GenAI adoption lies in disciplined, strategic execution that addresses the foundational issues of business alignment , trusted data and integrated design. To achieve meaningful results, organizations must move beyond pilots and embrace a strategic approach. Each initiative should be grounded in clearly defined, measurable objectives to ensure alignment with broader organizational goals. Invest in data foundations Without significant investment in data governance, quality, and infrastructure, it becomes nearly impossible to scale from experimentation to production in a meaningful way. documents.extractedContent: Email Template - Red Hat (AIOps:Turn Intelligence into Action) Last updated: February 2026 Purpose: Initiate discovery conversations  with IT Ops, SRE, Architects and Platforms struggling with alert fatigue, slow response, tech debt, and fragmentation across their monitoring & observability tools. Drive towards meetings that position Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) as the execution layer for AIOps- Turning AI insights into automated action Resources : Webinar: Scale your AI: Automation strategies for infrastructure and AIOps Ebook: Unlock the full potential of AIOps with automation Checklist: 5 practical AIOps use cases Webinar: AIOps Told You What's Wrong. Now What? Supercharge Your AI with Event-Driven Ansible! <w:pgSz w:h="15840" w:w="12240" w:orient="portrait"/><w:pgMar w:bottom="1440" w:top="1440" w:left="900" w:right="900" w:header="720" w:footer="720"/><w:cols w:equalWidth="0" w:num="1"><w:col w:space="0" w:w="10440"/></w:cols></w:sectPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:pict><v:rect style="width:0.0pt;height:1.5pt" o:hr="t" o:hrstd="t" o:hralign="center" fillcolor="#A0A0A0" stroked="f"/></w:pict></w:r><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr></w:r></w:p><w:p w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidP="00000000" w:rsidRDefault="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000" w14:paraId="0000000E"><w:pPr><w:spacing w:line="216" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="90" w:firstLine="0"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Red Hat Text" w:cs="Red Hat Text" w:eastAsia="Red Hat Text" w:hAnsi="Red Hat Text"/><w:sz w:val="16"/><w:szCs w:val="16"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr></w:r></w:p><w:p w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidP="00000000" w:rsidRDefault="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000" w14:paraId="0000000F"><w:pPr><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Red Hat Text" w:cs="Red Hat Text" w:eastAsia="Red Hat Text" w:hAnsi="Red Hat Text"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Red Hat Text" w:cs="Red Hat Text" w:eastAsia="Red Hat Text" w:hAnsi="Red Hat Text"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="24"/><w:szCs w:val="24"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Personas: CIO, CTO, IT Ops Leaders, SRE, Platform Engineer, Enterprise Architect Email #1 - Insight->Action Gap Subject Line: Are your AIOps tools driving real action? Hi {{first_name}}, Most teams have invested in AIOps and monitoring platforms. They detect issues faster — but remediation still takes time. That gap between detection and resolution is where MTTR expands and engineering hours disappear. Organizations are closing that gap by connecting AIOps insights directly to automated remediation with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform — turning alerts into standardized, governed action across hybrid environments. Instead of notifying engineers, the system can: Auto-resolve common incidents Enrich tickets with context Remediate drift before it spreads If improving MTTR without increasing headcount is a priority, is this worth a 20-minute discussion? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 - Alert Fatigue  , Slow Response Subject: Alert fatigue slowing down your team? Hi {{first_name}}, Curious if this sounds familiar for you and your team: Alert noise without clear signal on what actually requires action Incidents escalating across teams despite investments in monitoring and AIOps The same issues recurring because insights aren’t connected to automated resolution. Many teams tell us that they are generating more insights than ever, but still rely on manual steps to resolve issues. Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform is helping close that gap by automating the repetitive, predictable parts of incident response -  especially for common, high-volume issues that drain time. Can we speak Wednesday or Thursday of next week to see if automation potentially could reduce MTTR? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 - Tech Debt , Inconsistent Ops Subject: The hidden cost of repetitive incidents Hi {{first_name}}, A pattern we’re seeing: a lot of the operational cost in IT isn’t from major incidents -  it’s from the constant, repetitive fixes and triage that teams handle manually. Over time, that becomes tech debt and results in slower delivery and unnecessary outages. Teams are addressing this by connecting their AIOps tools directly to automation with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform That shift provides: Automated resolution of repetitive incidents to reduce manual effort Standardized, consistent remediation across environments Faster response with fewer errors without adding headcount I can walk through how other organizations are doing this and where it typically delivers the fastest wins. Can we find some time this week or next? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #4 - MTTR, Risk, Compliance (for Executives) Subject: Where teams are cutting MTTR without adding headcount Hi {{first_name}}, One theme from IT leaders lately: They're spending more time responding to incidents than preventing them. Even with strong AIOps tools, most teams still rely on manual remediation, which slows response time and increases operational risk. By combining AIOps with Ansible Automation Platform, teams are: Reducing MTTR significantly Eliminating drift-related outages Enforcing compliance automatically Improving resilience across environments It’s one of the few levers that improves reliability and reduces cost at the same time. If this aligns with what you’re working on, l et's connect next week. Would Tuesday or Thursday work for your schedule? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #5 - Proof Point, Ecosystem Subject: What customers are achieving with AIOps + Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform Hi {{first_name}}, A quick example: A customer recently connected their AIOps platform with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to auto-remediate the top recurring incidents, significantly reducing service downtime. They cut resolution time by 50% and eliminated thousands of manual tickets. Rather than replacing existing tools, Ansible Automation Platform integrates with observability platforms like Instana, Splunk, Dynatrace, LogicMonitor, and ServiceNow - turning insights from multiple sources into coordinated automated actions that fix drift, resolve config issues, and address performance problems before they impact users. If you're looking to see real results from your AIOps investments, I can share what leading organizations are doing today. Would {{time_option}} work for a short conversation? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: “How actionable are the insights coming out of your AIOps or monitoring tools today?” “What slows down response time the most once an issue is detected?” “Where do repetitive incidents consume the most time for your team?” “How often does configuration drift or misconfigurations cause problems?” “Do you have any automated remediation in place right now?” “How much time would your team save if 20–30% of incidents resolved themselves?” “Which tools are creating the most noise or alert fatigue?” “Do tickets come enriched with enough context for quick resolution?” “How consistent is the remediation process across your environments?” “Where do you see the biggest opportunity to reduce MTTR?” Additional Questions By Persona: IT Operations Leader/Director of IT Operations Use these to deepen discovery and tie AIOps → Action → Automation → MTTR reduction. Operational Efficiency “Which incidents or issues consume most of your operations time today?” “How long does it typically take to go from alert → diagnosis → fix?” “Where do manual steps slow things down the most?” AIOps + Observability Gaps “Are insights from your AIOps or monitoring tools actionable today?” “Do alerts come with enough context for your team to respond quickly?” “Which alerts would you automate first if you could?” Repetition + Process Consistency “Which problems does your team end up fixing more than once?” “How consistent is your remediation process across environments?” Risk + Drift “How often does configuration drift cause issues or outages?” “Do you have automated checks or enforcement for drift today?” Team Capacity “If repetitive incidents disappeared tomorrow, what would your team finally have time to focus on?” “Are you under pressure to improve MTTR without adding headcount?”

Automation Architect, Engineer / Sys Admin Email #1 Subject: What you know about AWX and Ansible Tower is wrong Hi {{first_name}}, Question: Are AWX, Ansible Tower, and Ansible Automation Platform essentially the same thing? Answer: No AWX = An unsupported collection of open source projects intended for testing and development only. Ansible Tower = A previous Red Hat solution that was last made generally available in 2019. Ansible Automation Platform = A full suite of enterprise-grade features that are supported and designed for ease of use and scale, including: Generative AI to help you manage and troubleshoot your automation and generate automation code fast. Automation analytics to help you measure and track your automation ROI, time savings, and performance. Self-service automation to help you extend automation to more users without sacrificing control. Event-driven automation to proactively respond to adverse events in your IT operations. Policy enforcement to help you maintain compliance and governance in an AIOps world. Ansible Automation Platform has a suite of new features that are worth a closer look. Are you available for a brief call next week to discuss? Best regards, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 Subject: 7 reasons why your IT automation is failing Hi {{first_name}}, This is {{sender.first_name}} from your extended team at Red Hat. I want to share the most common reasons we see too many organizations like yours fail to achieve their desired results with IT automation: Lack of executive sponsorship, strategy and roadmap for IT automation Inconsistent standards, governance, and tooling across teams Inability to execute cross-domain workflows that drive efficiency No formal measurement of automation ROI, time savings, etc. Too much control over automation given to a single team or individuals Resistance to change in tools and/or processes Maintenance of DIY tools like AWX that stifle productivity and innovation Can we set up a time to explore how Ansible Automation Platform and Red Hat can help you overcome these obstacles to innovation? Best regards, {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 Subject: Your IT automation is stealing your time Hi {{first_name}}, If you're using AWX to run your enterprise automation, you're spending time on management and maintenance that could be redirected towards innovation projects that drive your business forward–as opposed to just keeping the lights on. At Red Hat, we see time and time again that organizations that adopt the right solutions and approaches to automation are more productive, agile, and performative than their counterparts–and typically with lower TCO. Can we set up a time for me to share examples of organizations around the world who are automating at scale with success? Looking forward to your response! {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: What is your automation strategy? How do you ensure teams are acting in alignment with that strategy? Are you able to use a single unified tool to automate across multiple domains? Have you begun thinking about how your team will prepare for AI? What is in your plan so far? What’s getting in the way of you and an ideal, automated infrastructure? What are your top IT challenges? How do you measure automation performance? How are teams aligned? Are they collaborating or do they operate in silos? Are you using any free or community-based automation tools? How many automation tools are in use across all of IT? Are you still relying on manual scripting for patching and provisioning?

Subject Line: Streamline your NetOps processes Hi {{first_name}}, As network operations expand in scope, it is becoming more challenging to manage networks across hybrid cloud environments. To keep up with complex tasks that span from data centers to edge locations, network teams must turn to automated NetOps. Here are a few resources that show how organizations are using Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to orchestrate workflows across network and other domains for more efficient, resilient operations: Network automation guide for Ansible Automation Platform Checklist: 5 practical AIOps use cases 5 great use cases for Network Automation Let me know if you’d like to schedule a brief chat to see how we can help your organization. How does next {{weekdays_from_now 2}} or {{weekdays_from_now 3}} work for you? Thank you, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 Subject: The bigger picture - seeing real ROI from your automation investments Hi {{first_name}}, IT leaders are now asking their teams to show clearer ROI on their automation investments - especially as budgets get tighter. With Red Hat’s Ansible Automation platform, we can help teams: Automate network device configuration and management Apply consistent governance and security policies across your infrastructure Orchestrate complex workflows that span multiple domains (e.g., network, security, and cloud) I thought you might appreciate this , which details the financial benefits and business value our customers have seen. It is not about doing more - it's about getting more value from your automation. Can we schedule 15 minutes to discuss how we help teams position this for leadership consideration? {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 Subject: {{sender.first_name}}, how are you supporting your NetOps teams? {{first_name}}, How are you supporting the needs of rapidly shifting workload requirements for your business? Are your network teams keeping up with the demands of modern digital infrastructure? Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform can be used to automate entire network and IT processes across devices and domains - no matter if you are starting from scratch or scaling out. With automated NetOps, network engineers can use a variety of automation techniques to perform management and maintenance tasks, as well as respond automatically when conditions change across a network. Lets sync for 15 minutes to see how this could look in your organization, how does next {{weekdays_from_now 2}} look? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: If you’re nice and have extra brain power, a few conversation starters would be appreciated. Are you still relying on manual scripting for patching and provisioning?

Potential Cost Savings Opportunity for VMC and EC2 Dear ___________, We connected previously regarding VMC, and we wanted to share information about a significant cost savings opportunity related to it. Organizations can potentially achieve 30-60% annual cost savings by migrating their VMC and EC2 VMs to Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA). This is feasible because ROSA utilizes hardware overcommit, resulting in lower vCPU consumption per VM. Since ROSA is only purchased from AWS, it counts 100% toward your EDP, and I understand AWS has additional incentives specific to VMC migrations. ROSA lets you run both VMs and containers in the same unified platform, with scale and security. COMPANY NAME can keep running VM's as is, or modernize at your own pace with other integrated AWS native services. I've attached real customer cost savings examples, and AWS info about ROSA benefits below. Check out this vide o to learn more about how you can migrate your EC2 instances to OpenShift Virtualization on ROSA utilizing River Meadow. With your EC2 usage report, Red Hat can project potential cost savings, and then over a few days with your team, could do a $0 migration of 50 VM's to prove it before committing to anything. Let us know who we can work with on this, thanks. (Attach the AWS Cloud Cost Optimization 1-pager and AWS+RH Handout files as attachments)

This Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization’s ecosystem of partners provides businesses with flexibility in designing, migrating, and modernizing their virtualization solutions.

salesPlays.name: Build and Run Applications
salesPlays.description: The AI-Ready Enterprise sales play is a guide for positioning Red Hat as the trusted, open hybrid platform that enables enterprises to scale AI operations reliably and cost-effectively while maintaining control over their data, security, and choice of infrastructure.

pain: Use this to quickly understand customer priorities, desired outcomes, and how deals like this are won.
Their pain
AI models take too long to move into production
Rising infrastructure and GPU costs
Strict security, compliance, and data sovereignty requirements
Risk of vendor lock-in limiting flexibility
outcomes: Accelerate AI from experimentation → production
Reduce cost and optimize infrastructure usage
Ensure security, compliance, and data control
Maintain flexibility across hybrid and multi-cloud environments
impact: Faster innovation: months → minutes deployment
Lower total cost of AI: optimized compute + infrastructure
Reduced risk: secure, compliant, governed AI at scale
Greater flexibility: run AI anywhere, avoid lock-in

realWorldExamples.customer: ✈️ Turkish Airlines → Scaled 60+ AI models; reduced deployment from months to minutes
🚁 Airbus Helicopters → Lowered AI + infrastructure cost while maintaining control
🏦 DenizBank → Accelerated AI with built-in security and governance
☁️ Phoenix Systems → Delivered flexible, sovereign AI across hybrid environments
Pro tip: use the "what to share" section and send these references directly to your customers & track engagements.

painPoints: Scaling AI from pilot → production
Model performance + optimization
Reducing GPU / inference costs
ROI on AI investments
Risk, security and compliance
Governance across teams
Cost efficiency (GPU, compute)
Performance + scalability
Operational consistency
AI pilots working but not scaling
Fragmented tools across environments
No consistent pipeline from dev → prod
Fragmented AI initiatives
No centralized governance
Manual compliance + audits
Over-provisioned infrastructure
Limited visibility across environments
Manual operations
Delayed business impact
High compute costs
Slow AI delivery cycles
Wasted AI spend
Regulatory risk
Lack of trust in AI systems
High cloud + compute costs
Inefficiency at scale
Operational complexity
discoveryQuestions: “What’s slowing your AI from reaching production?”
“How are you managing inference costs at scale?”
“Where are models getting stuck today?”
“How are you governing AI across teams today?”
“What risks concern you most with AI adoption?”
“How are you measuring ROI on AI?”
“How are you managing GPU and compute costs today?”
“Where are you seeing inefficiencies?”
“How do you balance cost vs performance?”
valueProps: AI is expensive to run — not just to build. Once models move to production, GPU and cloud costs add up fast. Customers need a better way to manage resources and avoid wasted spend.
Complexity

As AI projects grow or move to the edge, where time-sensitive applications are vital or connectivity is limited, managing tools, pipelines, and models becomes complex. Teams struggle to keep everything consistent, secure, and running smoothly across environments.
Choice
Customers don’t want to get locked into one vendor’s AI stack. They want to choose the hardware, models, and cloud that work best for them — and switch when needed.
Cost optimization & efficiency
Run AI where it’s most cost-efficient — not where a vendor forces you. Maximize GPU and compute usage across environments.
Improve GPU and compute utilization and avoid waste
Run inference where it costs less — on-prem, in cloud, or edge
Standardize environments to eliminate duplicate spend and effort
Security & operational consistency
Secure and scale AI with the same tools and automation you already use for apps and infrastructure — no new silo.
Use one operating and automation model across data center and cloud
Automate patching, policy, model governance, and monitoring
Scale safely with repeatable, secure operations and guardrails
Flexibility & minimize lock-in
Keep freedom of choice as AI tools evolve — don’t bet your future on one cloud or model ecosystem.
Run and move AI across clouds and on-prem without re-platforming
Use open ecosystems — not proprietary AI stacks
Easily adopt new models or hardware as they evolve.
whatWinsThemOver: Faster path to production
Cost-efficient model serving
Consistent platform across environments
Governance + compliance baked in
Lower total cost of ownership
Flexibility (no lock-in)
Cost control + optimization
Automation + visibility
Flexibility across environments

salesPlays.name: Modernize Infrastructure
salesPlays.description: The IT Operations Efficiency sales play is a guide for positioning Red Hat as the trusted, open hybrid platform that helps customers simplify deployments, expand automation and unify day-2 operations—reducing cost, minimizing risk and freeing IT teams to focus on innovation across datacenter, cloud and edge.

pain: Use this to quickly understand customer priorities, desired outcomes, and how deals like this are won.
Their pain
Manual, repetitive operational tasks slow delivery and consume valuable IT resources
Tool sprawl and inconsistent processes increase complexity, drift, and risk
Rising cloud and operational costs strain budgets and reduce efficiency
Limied visibility and reactive incident response make it hard to scale reliably
outcomes: Standardize and automate operations across hybrid environments
Reduce manual work and free capacity for higher-value initiatives
Improve visibility, governance, and incident response across operations
Optimize cloud and infrastructure costs while maintaining reliability
impact: Unlock capacity for innovation: free teams from repetitive tasks to focus on strategic work
Lower total cost: reduce cloud waste, manual remediation, and operational overhead
Reduced risk: improve governance, compliance, and operational resilience
Faster response: reduce MTTR and improve service reliability with automated remediation

realWorldExamples.customer: 🏢 Ensono → Reallocated 21,000+ hours of manual work annually through automation
💄 Ulta Beauty → Reduced deployment cycles from weeks to hours, saving millions in operational costs
✈️ CAE → Built a secure, automated operations backbone with improved audit readiness and reliability

painPoints: Lowering operating costs and reducing cloud waste
Improving operational consistency and reliability
Freeing teams from manual work to focus on innovation
Simplifying operations and reducing tool sprawl
Faster remediation and incident response
Reducing cloud waste caused by misconfigurations
Scaling operations without increasing headcount
Maintaining consistent patterns for developers
Reducing manual operational work that slows delivery
Rising operating costs and inefficient processes
Too much firefighting, not enough strategic work
Inconsistent operations create outages, customer impact, and risk
Too many disconnected tools and inconsistent deployments
Manual provisioning leads to configuration drift

Manual work slows application and platform delivery

Increased OPEX and wasted cloud spend
Slower delivery of new business initiatives
Higher risk of downtime and compliance gaps
Increased downtime and operational inefficiency
Higher infrastructure and cloud costs
Teams spend more time managing issues than preventing them
Slower developer productivity and onboarding
Increased operational noise and drift
Difficulty scaling services reliably
discoveryQuestions: Where are operational inconsistencies creating risk and driving up costs?
How much time do teams spend on reactive work vs. strategic work?
How do you enforce standards across datacenter, cloud, and edge?
How consistent are your deployments across all environments?
What slows down remediation when issues occur?
Where are you seeing cloud waste today?
How do you standardize how applications run across clusters?
What operational tasks are still manual?
How do you minimize drift and maintain reliability at scale?
valueProps: Customers are under pressure to reduce operational costs, eliminate manual work, and simplify fragmented tools and processes across hybrid environments.
Complexity
Customers need consistent, secure, and compliant operations across datacenter, cloud, and edge while reducing drift and human error.
Choice
Customers need better visibility across environments and faster ways to detect, triage, and remediate issues before they impact the business.
Cost & Capacity

Red Hat standardizes operations and automates repetitive tasks across IT domains, reducing operational overhead and freeing teams to focus on innovation. With unified automation and consistent operating environments, customers improve utilization and reduce waste.
Security & Operational Consistency

Red Hat provides policy-driven automation, standardized baselines, and governance across environments. This reduces configuration drift, improves compliance, and creates more predictable, resilient operations.
Visibility, Speed & Resilience
Red Hat enables event-driven automation and unified management across hybrid environments to improve visibility, reduce MTTR, and create self-healing operations that scale reliably.
whatWinsThemOver: Standardized deployments and governance across environments
Automated remediation and policy-based operations
Reduced downtime, improved reliability, and freed capacity for innovation
Consistent deployment patterns across environments
Automated remediation and faster incident response
Policy-based governance to reduce cloud waste and improve efficiency
A stable, predictable operating layer
Automated governance and event-driven remediation
Faster delivery with less operational complexity

salesPlays.name: The AI-Ready Enterprise
salesPlays.description: is no longer just a geopolitical concern—it is a strategic business imperative driven by the

pain: Their pain
Increasing regulatory and compliance requirements (GDPR, AI Act, NIS2, etc.)
Risk of vendor lock-in with hyperscalers and proprietary platforms
Lack of control over data location, access, and jurisdiction
Rising geopolitical and cybersecurity risks impacting operations and trust
Limited visibility and transparency into software supply chains
outcomes: Maintain full control over data, infrastructure, and operations
Ensure compliance with evolving global and regional regulations
Reduce dependency on any single vendor or jurisdiction
Improve transparency, auditability, and security across the stack
Enable innovation (including AI) without compromising sovereignty
impact: Reduced risk: mitigate regulatory, legal, and geopolitical exposure
Increased trust: ensure data control, transparency, and compliance
Greater flexibility: run workloads anywhere while avoiding lock-in
Sustained innovation: enable AI and digital transformation within sovereign constraints
Red Hat examples
☁️ Phoenix Systems → Built a Swiss sovereign cloud to deliver secure, compliant, in-region services and reduce geopolitical risk
🌏 NxtGen → Delivered sovereign AI infrastructure with full control over data, models, and compliance across hybrid environments
🏦 Emirates NBD → Launched a cloud-native banking platform meeting strict regulatory requirements while accelerating innovation and time-to-market
Pro tip: use the "what to share" section and send these references directly to your customers & track engagements.

painPoints: Regulatory compliance and risk mitigation
Data control and operational resilience
Balancing cost with sovereignty requirements
Avoiding vendor lock-in and long-term risk
Ensuring cost-effective, compliant vendor selection
Transparency in vendor technology and contracts
Building a consistent platform across sovereign environments
Managing complexity across multiple clouds and regions
Ensuring security, compliance, and scalability
Complex and evolving regulations create uncertainty
Limited control over data and infrastructure in cloud environments
Increasing pressure from board and regulators
Concern about dependence on hyperscalers
